name: Basilica of St. Paul
history: The first Catholics came to Daytona Beach in 1881, and the first resident priest arrived in 1895 and built a church in 1898. The present church was completed in 1927 for about $250,000. It was named a basilica in 2006.
arch: Mission Revival by Chicago architect Gerald A. Barry, with an ornate carved central front. When built, it was the tallest building on the mainland.
features: It was one of the first buildings in the area with central heating and air conditioning.
A fresco of the conversion of St. Paul is above the altar.

look.d: A richly carved Spanish-style centre panel frames the door.
The cupola and cross on top date from 2006.

fun: Air conditioning in 1927 Florida was a minor miracle of its own.
journal: Spanish curls and a sea breeze. Daytona's tallest building, once.
